overall: The AG found the Cape Cod Commission Executive Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law on any of the three allegations: the executive session purpose, the executive session notice topic, and the missing 'open session' listing.

allegations.summary: Executive session under Purpose 1 to discuss an OML complaint against the committee was improper, since Purpose 1 covers only complaints against individuals.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the executive session discussion that occurred did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The notice's executive session topic, referencing a complaint about the April 30 meeting, was not specific enough to inform the public.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the executive session topic listed was sufficiently specific to inform the public that the Committee would be meeting in executive session

allegations.summary: The notice failed to list 'open session' as a topic before the executive session topic.
allegations.key_passage: Committee was not required to also list "open session" as a topic in its notice, and did not violate the Open Meeting Law by not doing so.

source.publisher_filename: DETERMINATION - 7 27 2015 - OML 2015-105 - CAPE COD COMMISSION EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE.pdf
